Not just the electric bill. The inverter comes from the highest simultaneous load in the timeline, the battery from night use, and the panels from the energy needed per day. Common appliances are preloaded; delete what you do not have and add your own.

Your household type iTypical household: the usual home pattern scaled to the bill. Operating hours: for shops, courts, offices and other businesses. The bill's kWh is spread over the hours each facility is open (flat while open), plus a small always-on base load. Use "Share of bill" when one facility uses more than its hours suggest; leave it on Auto to split by hours.

Brownout iWhat happens when the grid is down all day: solar and the battery only. Set the energy the outage needs as a share of the daily use shown in the appliance list (for example 30% of 77.3 kWh = 23.2 kWh), when it starts and how long it lasts. With a start time, that energy is spread over the outage hours following the load's own pattern. "All day" repeats a full day with the grid down; a start time shows one outage on an average day, starting from the usual 6AM battery level. The red part of the graph is load the system can't carry. Display only: the battery is still sized for the usual loads.
